participants.role: Announces the rule and gives its reason when asked

participants.role: Challenges the process, then accepts a compromise
participants.trajectory: Objects twice to how the rule was made, then accepts a way to keep his key
alternatives: His objection may be to losing his own key more than to the process

participants.tone: Polite in form, firm in substance
participants.role: Defends the rule by pointing to the record
participants.trajectory: Speaks once in the dispute, with a reply that raises tension
alternatives: The reply may have been meant as information rather than as a rebuke

participants.role: Asks for the reason, which opens the clarification
participants.trajectory: One question that shifts the exchange from process to purpose

events.speaker: nell
events.quotation: From Monday the shed key lives in the lockbox - code goes out tonight.
events.context: The first message of the evening
events.interpretation: Announces a change as already settled
events.contribution: Sets the subject and its terms

sentiment.label: neutral
sentiment.basis: Plain statement with no emotional wording

tension.basis: No disagreement yet; the settled framing leaves room for one

events.speaker: felix
events.quotation: Nobody asked us. I've had a key for six years.
events.context: The first reply beyond an emoji
events.interpretation: Objects to how the rule was made and claims standing by long use
events.contribution: Opens the dispute and frames it as one of process

sentiment.label: aggrieved
sentiment.basis: Complaint of exclusion and appeal to his own record

events.speaker: tobias
events.quotation: It was in last month's minutes, Felix.
events.interpretation: Rebuts the process complaint by pointing to the record
events.contribution: Turns the challenge into a dispute between two members

tension.basis: Rejects the complaint and addresses Felix by name, which raises the stakes despite the polite form

events.inference: Tobias may have read Felix's complaint as an accusation against the committee

events.speaker: felix
events.interpretation: Rejects the record as a form of consultation
events.contribution: The peak of the dispute; names consultation as the real issue

tension.basis: Flat rejection of the other side's answer

events.speaker: saoirse
events.quotation: Can I check - is this about the missing strimmer?
events.context: The first voice from outside the dispute
events.interpretation: Asks for the reason behind the rule
events.contribution: Moves the exchange from who decided to why

sentiment.label: anxious
sentiment.basis: Tentative opening and mention of a loss

tension.basis: A question rather than a position; lowers the temperature

events.speaker: nell
events.quotation: Partly. Mostly insurance wants a log of who goes in.
events.interpretation: Gives an outside requirement as the reason
events.contribution: Supplies the purpose the announcement lacked

events.speaker: hamid
events.quotation: Could Felix keep his key and just sign the log too?

events.interpretation: Proposes a way to meet the insurer's need without taking Felix's key

sentiment.label: conciliatory
sentiment.basis: Constructive question addressed to both sides

tension.basis: A proposal that answers both positions

events.speaker: greta
events.quotation: Shall we put the lockbox idea to the March meeting properly?
events.interpretation: Proposes proper consultation on the rule
events.contribution: Answers the process complaint without reopening the dispute

tension.basis: Agreed at once by the rule's announcer

phases.label: Opening

phases.label: Challenge
phases.description: Felix objects to how the rule was made

phases.label: Escalation
phases.description: The record is offered and rejected as consultation

phases.label: Clarification
phases.description: A question brings out the insurer's reason

phases.label: Mediation
phases.description: A compromise keeps Felix's key with a log

phases.label: Resolution, partial

takeaways.text: The tension was about process, consultation, more than about the rule itself
A question about purpose, not a defence of the rule, turned the exchange
Polite wording raised tension and anxious wording lowered it: sentiment and tension moved apart

overall.character: A short dispute about how a rule was made, resolved for now by a compromise and a promise of proper consultation
tension_sources: An announcement made without visible consultation
The minutes offered as consultation and rejected
uncertainties: Whether the March meeting will keep the lockbox rule
Whether a strimmer is in fact missing
alternatives: The exchange can also be read as one member's attachment to his own key, with the process complaint as its form
